mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.2%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.2% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE above 8.5%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST above 450) and retail sales (RSAFS above 380,000) indicates strong consumer demand that boosts corporate revenues, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive SPX returns in more than 50% of cases over a 2-year rolling window (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO above 100) indicates expanding manufacturing activity that increases corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 100 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A growing GDP (GDPC1 above 13,300) indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive (year-over-year) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL annualized growth above 2.5%) signals potential monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment (UNRATE below 8.5%) and employment growth (PAYEMS above 130,000) indicate a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of falling UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to predict positive SPX returns in more than 50% of cases over a 2-year rolling window (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing market expansion (HOUST above 450) drives consumer confidence and retail activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in housing-driven demand regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 450 over a 3-year rolling window.
